lesson.text: Quick memory: which city does the Prime Meridian, 0° longitude, run through? (London, at Greenwich.) When it is lunchtime in London, it is night in New Zealand. Today: why, and how time zones work.

Earth spins once every 24 hours. The half facing the Sun has day; the other half has night. As Earth turns towards the east, the Sun seems to rise in the east and set in the west. Here it is noon at Greenwich.
A full turn is 360°. In 24 hours, 360 ÷ 24 = 15, so Earth turns 15° of longitude every hour. A place 15° east of you sees sunrise, noon and sunset an hour earlier than you do.

So the world is split into time zones, each about 15° wide, counted from Greenwich. Places to the east are ahead of London: their clocks show a later time. Places to the west are behind: their clocks show an earlier time.

Zone borders bend to follow countries. China is very wide but uses one time for the whole country. In January, India is 5½ hours ahead of London, and some countries move their clocks an hour forward in summer.
In January, when it is 12:00 in London, Tokyo is 9 hours ahead: 12 + 9 = 21, so it is 21:00. New York is 5 hours behind: 12 − 5 = 7, so it is 07:00 in the morning.

Near the 180° line runs the International Date Line. Cross it going west and the calendar jumps a day ahead; going east, it goes back a day. The world agreed on the Prime Meridian at Greenwich in 1884.
Try it in the world: make a wall of three clocks labelled London, Tokyo and New York, and set each one right when London shows 12:00. Next: climate zones.

exercises.prompt: How long does Earth take to spin round once?
exercises.hint: One spin gives one day and one night.
exercises.explain: About 24 hours: one day and one night.

exercises.prompt: When it is day on one side of Earth, it is night on the other.
exercises.hint: Only one half faces the Sun at a time.
exercises.explain: True: the half facing the Sun has day, and the other half has night.

exercises.prompt: In which direction does the Sun seem to rise?
exercises.hint: Think of a compass with north at the top: the morning Sun appears on the right.
exercises.explain: The Sun seems to rise in the east and set in the west.

exercises.prompt: Places east of London have clocks that are...
exercises.hint: Places to the east see the Sun first.
exercises.explain: Ahead: places to the east see the Sun earlier, so their clocks show a later time.

exercises.prompt: Earth turns 15° of longitude every hour.
It is 10:00 in London. Cairo is 2 hours ahead. What time is it in Cairo?
exercises.hint: Ahead means a later time: add the hours.

exercises.prompt: It is 15:00 in London. New York is 5 hours behind. What time is it in New York?
exercises.hint: Behind means an earlier time: take the hours away.
exercises.explain: 15 − 5 = 10, so it is 10:00 in New York.

exercises.prompt: Sort these cities: ahead of London or behind it?
exercises.hint: East of Greenwich is ahead; west is behind. Use the table.
exercises.explain: Ahead: Tokyo, Beijing, Cairo. Behind: New York, Los Angeles, Lima.

exercises.prompt: China uses one time for the whole country.
exercises.explain: True: China is very wide but uses a single time.

exercises.prompt: In January, how many hours ahead of London is India? Type it as a decimal.
exercises.hint: India is 5½ hours ahead. Half an hour is 0.5 of an hour.

exercises.prompt: It is 20:00 in London. Tokyo is 9 hours ahead. What time is it in Tokyo?
exercises.hint: Add the hours. If you pass midnight, it is the next day.

exercises.prompt: A town is at 60°E. How many hours ahead of Greenwich is its Sun time?
Why do time zone borders bend?
exercises.hint: Would a country like its towns to have different times?
exercises.explain: Borders bend so a country, or part of one, can keep the same time.

exercises.prompt: A plane crosses the International Date Line going west. What happens to the date?
exercises.hint: Remember: west across the line, a day ahead.
exercises.explain: Going west across the Date Line, the calendar jumps a day ahead.

exercises.prompt: Tokyo is 9 hours ahead of London; New York is 5 hours behind London. How many hours ahead of New York is Tokyo?
exercises.hint: Count from New York up to London, then on to Tokyo.
exercises.explain: 5 hours from New York to London, then 9 more to Tokyo: 5 + 9 = 14 hours.

exercises.prompt: It is 12:00 in London in January. Match each place to its time.
exercises.hint: Add the hours for places ahead, and take them away for places behind.
exercises.explain: Tokyo: 12 + 9 = 21, so 21:00. New York: 12 − 5 = 7, so 07:00. Cairo: 12 + 2 = 14, so 14:00. India: 5½ hours ahead makes 17:30.
